transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, doc, I just... I mean, I had to come in because I just can't take it anymore. It's like... you know how an old truck sounds when you just leave it idling in the driveway? Just humming and vibrating? That's what's inside me. I feel like I got this motor running inside me all day long. From the second I open my eyes, it's just going and going. 

And if I have to sit still for even a little bit—like, say, at church. My family wants me to sit there in the pew for an hour, but I just feel like my skin is crawling and I'm completely trapped. Or even just out there in your waiting room at the clinic today! I felt so boxed in just waiting for my name to be called. I kept having to stand up, you know, walk over to the water fountain, look out the window, pace the hallway... I just have to get up or do something. I can't help it. 

Even at home, I can't just sit on the couch and watch a show like a normal person. I feel trapped right there in my own living room, like a caged animal or something, and I just have to be moving or messing with something. It's just this constant, running, humming feeling, and I don't know how to shut the engine off, and it's just... it's driving me crazy, you know?
Did you have similar trouble sitting still or feeling overly restless when you were a child?

Oh, man, did I ever. It ain't just a new thing, doc, it's... it's been like this my whole life, I swear. I remember back when I was just a boy in school—which, you know, I didn't even make it to high school because of all this—but back in the day, it was a total nightmare. 

The teachers, they were always, and I mean *always*, moving my seat around. Like every other week they had me at a new desk. They'd stick me in the front row, then banish me to the back corner, then put me right up against the chalkboard next to them. They did it because I just could not stay put to save my life. I'd be up out of my chair, wandering around, or I'd be talking completely out of turn right in the middle of a lesson. I just couldn't hold it in, you know? If I thought of something, I just said it, I couldn't stop myself. 

And the worst part was getting to the end of the day, or even just the end of a period. I got in so much trouble for jumping up before class was even done. The bell hadn't even rung yet, the teacher was still talking, and I was already up on my feet, grabbing my stuff, just ready to bolt out that door because I couldn't take sitting there for one more second. They used to call my folks all the time complaining about it, saying I was a disruption and all that. But I wasn't trying to be bad! It was just... sitting at those little hard desks all day was pure torture for me, and my body just wouldn't let me do it.
